primitives.name: Inertial Navigation Module
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system includes an inertial navigation system (INS) module first state module adapted for measuring parameters associated with the object state, a wireless transmitter, a battery for providing electric power, and a mounting module connecting the object with the first state module, the wireless transmitter and the battery.
primitives.assumptions: Constant motion model; negligible external forces during short intervals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High acceleration or rotation rates exceeding sensor dynamic range.

layer2.mapping: INS-derived kinematic state serves as prior in GSE state transition kernel and GSI posterior update.

primitives.name: Camera Tracking System
primitives.verbatim_quote: The camera system capturing the object includes at least two mutually displaced camera clusters, and each camera cluster includes one or more cameras for providing a predetermined spatial resolution.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I(x,y,t)': 'image intensity at pixel (x,y) at time t', 'K': 'camera intrinsic matrix (dimensionless)', 'R(t), T(t)': 'rotation and translation at time t', 'u,v': 'image coordinates (pixels)'}
primitives.assumptions: Known camera calibration; object visibility and distinct features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Occlusion, low-light conditions, or featureless surfaces.

layer2.mapping: Visual feature correspondence maps to GSE pose estimation via projective geometry.
layer2.telemetry: Image sequence from stereo camera clusters

primitives.name: GPS Positioning Module
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system may include a global positioning system (GPS) module which provides the independent data relating to the object state.
primitives.assumptions: Line-of-sight to satellites; minimal atmospheric delay.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Urban canyon effect, indoor environments, or signal jamming.

layer2.mapping: GPS fixes provide ground-truth anchor points for GSE localization and GSI error correction.

The core innovation lies in fusing inertial, visual, and GPS data streams to reconstruct object state in real time. The INS module provides high-frequency kinematic estimates but drifts over time. The camera system offers geometric constraints through image-based triangulation, enabling robust pose recovery despite occlusions. The GPS module supplies absolute reference positions, correcting long-term drift. These modalities form a dualistic structure where INS acts as a predictor, camera as a verifier, and GPS as a calibrator. Failure modes arise when any modality fails—e.g., GPS loss leads to drift, camera occlusion breaks geometric consistency, and INS saturation causes integration errors. The system's resilience depends on cross-validation and adaptive weighting of sensor inputs. Mathematical duality emerges in how each sensor type encodes complementary aspects of motion: translational (INS, GPS) vs. rotational (INS, camera) and spatial (camera, GPS) vs. temporal (INS) dynamics.
